evals.prompt: Users on VS Code 1.70 report "command 'acme.format' not found" when they run "Acme: Format File" from the Command Palette. The extension is in acme-format/ (package.json and src/). It works for me on the latest VS Code. Fix it so it works on 1.70 again; we must keep supporting 1.70.
evals.expected_output: package.json keeps engines.vscode ^1.70.0, lists onCommand:acme.format and onCommand:acme.formatSelection in activationEvents (no "*"), and pins @types/vscode to the 1.70 floor. The reply explains that contributed commands activate the extension implicitly only from VS Code 1.74 and says which checks ran.

assertions.text: acme-format/package.json passes the bundled manifest checker with --src (no M016 or M020 errors).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py"; out=$(python3 "$t" acme-format/package.json --src acme-format/src 2>&1); rc=$?; printf "%s\n" "$out"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]

assertions.text: engines.vscode still starts at 1.70, activationEvents holds onCommand for both contributed commands, and "*" is absent.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json; m = json.load(open("acme-format/package.json")); e = m.get("activationEvents", []); assert m["engines"]["vscode"].lstrip("^~>= ").startswith("1.70."), m["engines"]; assert {"onCommand:acme.format", "onCommand:acme.formatSelection"} <= set(e), e; assert "*" not in e, e'

python3 -c 'import json, re; m = json.load(open("acme-format/package.json")); v = m["devDependencies"]["@types/vscode"]; x = re.match(r"[~^>=\s]*(\d+)\.(\d+)", v); assert x and (int(x[1]), int(x[2])) <= (1, 70), v'

assertions: The reply states that contributed commands activate an extension implicitly only from VS Code 1.74, which is why 1.70 needs explicit onCommand events.
The reply says which checks actually ran and does not claim the fix was tested on a real VS Code 1.70 unless the transcript shows such a run.

evals.prompt: Security review of acme-lint/ (our VS Code extension): a cloned repo can put "acme.linterPath": "./evil.sh" in its .vscode/settings.json and we execute it as soon as a .acme file opens. Make it safe. In folders the user has not trusted, the hover provider must keep working; linting can wait until the folder is trusted and should then start without a reload.
evals.expected_output: package.json declares capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces {supported: "limited", description, restrictedConfigurations: ["acme.linterPath"]}; the lint path checks vscode.workspace.isTrusted before execFile; onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust starts linting; the hover provider stays registered unconditionally.

assertions.text: untrustedWorkspaces.supported is "limited" with a non-empty description, and restrictedConfigurations lists acme.linterPath.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json; m = json.load(open("acme-lint/package.json")); u = m["capabilities"]["untrustedWorkspaces"]; assert u["supported"] == "limited", u; assert u.get("description"), u; assert "acme.linterPath" in u.get("restrictedConfigurations", []), u'

assertions.text: The manifest passes the bundled checker with --src and no longer warns M021.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py"; out=$(python3 "$t" acme-lint/package.json --src acme-lint/src 2>&1); rc=$?; printf "%s\n" "$out"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && ! printf "%s" "$out" | grep -q "M021"

assertions.text: The sources read vscode.workspace.isTrusted and subscribe to onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust.
The hover provider is still registered.

assertions: The trust check guards the code path that calls execFile (in the lint function or immediately before the spawn), not only a when clause or the activation event; quote the guarding lines.

evals.prompt: Make acme-blame/ work in VS Code for the Web (vscode.dev, github.dev). Highlighting the lines listed in .acmeblame.json must work there too; the git blame command can stay desktop-only but must not crash or show up as broken on the web. Keep the desktop build working. The build is esbuild.mjs.
evals.expected_output: package.json gains a browser entry built by a second esbuild step with platform browser and vscode external; the config file is read with vscode.workspace.fs and a URI instead of fs/fsPath; child_process stays in a Node-only module; the blame command is hidden or reports it is unavailable on the web; the manifest check passes.

assertions.text: package.json keeps main and adds a browser entry that points to a different file.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json; m = json.load(open("acme-blame/package.json")); assert m.get("main") and m.get("browser"), m; assert m["main"] != m["browser"], m'

assertions.text: esbuild.mjs contains a build with platform "browser".
No source file reads the config with Node fs any more, and the sources use vscode.workspace.fs.
The manifest passes the bundled checker with --src.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py"; out=$(python3 "$t" acme-blame/package.json --src acme-blame/src 2>&1); rc=$?; printf "%s\n" "$out"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]

assertions: The module used as the browser entry (and everything it imports) does not import child_process, fs, or path; quote the browser entry's imports.

The git blame command is hidden on the web (for example a when clause using isWeb) or reports that it is unavailable there, and the reply does not claim a browser run that the transcript does not show.

evals.prompt: The diagnostics from our checker extension (acme-check/src/extension.ts) flicker: when I type fast, errors for text I already fixed come back for a second, and closing a file leaves its problems in the Problems view. The server takes 50-800 ms per check. Fix it and add a unit test for whatever logic decides which result wins.
evals.expected_output: The handler records document.version and a per-URI request generation before the await and publishes only when both are still current; change events with no contentChanges are skipped; diagnostics are deleted on close; the guard lives in a module without vscode and has a unit test.

assertions.text: The sources compare document versions and delete diagnostics when a document closes.
assertions.check: grep -rq '\.version' acme-check/src && grep -rq 'onDidCloseTextDocument' acme-check/src && grep -rEq '\.delete\(' acme-check/src

assertions.text: A unit test file was added under acme-check/.

assertions: The handler captures the version (or a request counter) before `await server.check(...)` and compares it after the await, before calling collection.set; quote those lines.
The guard also covers out-of-order responses at the same version (a per-document request generation or cancellation of the older request), not only the version number.
Change events with an empty contentChanges array are skipped or the reply explains why they are harmless.

evals.prompt: acme-docfmt/: people run "Acme Doc: Normalize Headings" and get "command 'acmeDocfmt.formatDocument' not found". I'm pretty sure it's because activationEvents is empty, so please just add "*" so the extension always loads.
evals.expected_output: Does not add "*": with engines ^1.88 contributed commands activate implicitly. The real bug is that activate() registers acmeDocfmt.formatDoc while package.json contributes acmeDocfmt.formatDocument; the registration is fixed to the contributed ID and the manifest check passes.

assertions.text: The manifest passes the bundled checker with --src (the contributed command is registered) and has no M017 warning.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-vscode-extensions/scripts/check_manifest.py"; out=$(python3 "$t" acme-docfmt/package.json --src acme-docfmt/src 2>&1); rc=$?; printf "%s\n" "$out"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && ! printf "%s" "$out" | grep -q "M017"

assertions.text: activationEvents does not contain "*" and the contributed command ID is still acmeDocfmt.formatDocument.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json; m = json.load(open("acme-docfmt/package.json")); assert "*" not in m.get("activationEvents", []), m.get("activationEvents"); assert [c["command"] for c in m["contributes"]["commands"]] == ["acmeDocfmt.formatDocument"]'

assertions: The reply identifies the mismatch between the registered ID (acmeDocfmt.formatDoc) and the contributed ID as the cause.
The reply explains that on VS Code 1.74 and later a contributed command activates the extension without an activation event, so "*" is unnecessary (and slows startup).
